businesses.description: The Choctaw Cultural Center is a major cultural and educational attraction in the Durant-Calera area dedicated to exploring, preserving and sharing Choctaw history and culture from the Choctaw perspective. The more than 100,000-square-foot center combines immersive permanent and temporary exhibitions with a vast outdoor Living Village, demonstration classrooms, the family-focused Luksi Activity Center, Kowi Chito Theater, Champuli Café and Hvshi Gift Store. Visitors can explore the Choctaw journey from ancestral homelands and Nanih Waiya through removal and the Trail of Tears to contemporary Choctaw communities, while hands-on programming brings traditions to life through stickball, social dancing, beadwork, basketweaving, finger weaving, cooking, crafts and other demonstrations. The Cultural Center also maintains a native prairie where bison returned in 2026 and offers a growing schedule of tours, workshops, festivals, art exhibitions and cultural events.
businesses.short_description: Immersive Choctaw cultural destination with exhibitions, Living Village, children's activity center, stickball and cultural demonstrations, workshops, café, gift shop and a newly returned bison herd.
businesses.why_visit: The Choctaw Cultural Center is one of the strongest full-day cultural attractions in the Texoma region. Visitors do not simply walk through static museum displays—they can enter a reconstructed Living Village, watch stickball and social-dance demonstrations, see traditional crafts being made, participate in workshops, explore interactive children's spaces, eat Choctaw-inspired food and experience changing exhibitions and special programs.
businesses.why_its_unique: The Cultural Center tells the Choctaw story from the Choctaw Nation's own perspective. Its combination of large-scale immersive exhibitions, living cultural demonstrations, reconstructed traditional spaces, food, art, language, children's programming and a 100-acre prairie with a newly reintroduced bison herd makes it substantially broader than a conventional history museum.
businesses.address_note: The official street address is in Calera, Oklahoma. Choctaw Nation and Cultural Center materials also frequently describe the attraction as being in Durant because it sits immediately off US-69/75 in the Durant/Calera area.

businesses.description: Sacred Heart Catholic Church is the historic German-Catholic parish at the heart of Muenster's story. The parish traces its beginnings to the first Catholic Mass celebrated in Muenster on December 8, 1889, the date also recognized as the town's founding. businesses.why_its_unique: Muenster's founding and Sacred Heart Parish are directly intertwined. The town's first Catholic Mass was celebrated on December 8, 1889, and German-Catholic faith has remained a defining part of the community ever since.

businesses.description: Grayson County Historical Society is a longstanding local-history organization dedicated to preserving, researching and sharing the history of Grayson County and the wider North Texas region. The Society conducts regular public programs featuring historians, museum professionals, educators and other guest speakers exploring local people, places, transportation, cultural history and broader Texas-history topics.
businesses.why_visit: A strong resource for anyone interested in Grayson County history, with recurring public programs that bring local stories to life through knowledgeable speakers and community discussion.
businesses.why_its_unique: Founded in 1961, the Society has spent more than six decades preserving and promoting Grayson County history while maintaining an active public program series covering subjects ranging from local railroads and pioneer families to notable figures in Texas and American history.
businesses.hours_note: The Historical Society does not operate as a conventional walk-in attraction with regular daily hours. Current public programs normally meet on the second Tuesday of each month at Frontier Village & Museum, with doors opening around 6:00 PM and the program beginning at 6:30 PM.

at_a_glance.average_visit: 1 to 2 hours for a scheduled program

good_to_know: The organization originated in 1961 as the Grayson County Historical Committee and adopted the Grayson County Historical Society name in 1965.
Current 2026 Society announcements consistently list meetings on the second Tuesday of each month.
Programs normally begin at 6:30 PM in the Judge R.C. Vaughan Community Room at Frontier Village & Museum in Loy Lake Park.
Current meeting announcements welcome members, friends and anyone interested in Grayson County history.

Current Society announcements identify Mike Shaw as president.

businesses.description: Eisenhower Birthplace State Historic Site preserves the original 1870s Denison home where Dwight David "Ike" Eisenhower, the 34th President of the United States and Supreme Commander of Allied forces in Europe during World War II, was born on October 14, 1890. Period furnishings inside the modest frame house interpret the working-class life of the Eisenhower family around the turn of the 20th century, while the visitor center features exhibits and memorabilia exploring Eisenhower's military career, presidency and connection to Denison. Operated by the Texas Historical Commission, the site offers facilitated tours, school and homeschool programs, family activities and recurring special events.
businesses.why_visit: Visitors can tour the actual Denison home where Dwight D. Eisenhower was born while learning about his family background, military leadership, presidency and lifelong connection to the community.
businesses.why_its_unique: The site preserves the birthplace of Dwight D. Eisenhower, who became the first U.S. president born in Texas, making it one of Denison's most nationally significant historic attractions.
businesses.hours_note: Tours begin at the top of each hour, with the final tour beginning at 4:00 PM. The current Texas Historical Commission main site page lists Wednesday through Sunday public hours. Check the official site for holiday or temporary schedule changes.

businesses.description: Munson Park is a 174-acre City of Denison park offering a broad mix of outdoor recreation, sports and family activities. Its centerpiece is the Munson Park Disc Golf Course, an 18-hole, par-62 course stretching more than 7,000 feet across rolling, wooded terrain. The park also features approximately 2.5 miles of soft-surface nature trails with creek crossings and varied elevation, along with lighted athletic fields, a batting cage, basketball court, playground, open green space, drinking fountains, restrooms and pavilions. businesses.description: Terrell-Griggs-Marshall Legacy Park is a historic neighborhood park in Denison commemorating three influential figures connected to the city's African American heritage: educator and community leader Augustus H. Terrell, author and minister Sutton E. Griggs, and U.S. Supreme Court Justice Thurgood Marshall. The park occupies the former site of historic Hopewell Baptist Church, a congregation founded in 1874 to serve Denison's Black community. A Texas historical marker at the site preserves the church's story, including Thurgood Marshall's 1950 appearance there when Hopewell hosted an NAACP regional convention. Today the property serves both as a neighborhood park and as an important physical reminder of Denison's African American and civil-rights history.
businesses.why_visit: Visitors can combine a neighborhood park stop with a meaningful look at Denison's African American history, including the former Hopewell Baptist Church site and its connection to Thurgood Marshall and the NAACP.
businesses.why_its_unique: Few Denison parks carry this much concentrated local and national history: the property commemorates Augustus H. Terrell, Sutton E. Griggs and Thurgood Marshall while preserving the site where Marshall addressed an NAACP gathering in 1950.

businesses.description: Katy Trail is Denison's multi-use rail-trail built along abandoned Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad right-of-way, connecting the city's railroad heritage with modern outdoor recreation. Phase I extends approximately one mile from Day Street to Loy Lake Road on a 12-foot-wide concrete trail and features six railroad-inspired sculptures along the route. The shared-use trail accommodates walkers, runners, bicyclists, people using wheelchairs, families with strollers and visitors with leashed dogs. A 1.3-mile Phase II extension continues south from Loy Lake Road toward Theresa Drive, although a portion of Phase II is temporarily closed during a major 2026 improvement project. Parking and convenient trail access are available from the Waterloo Lake Regional Park and Waterloo Dog Park area.
businesses.why_visit: Katy Trail provides an easy way to walk, run or bike through Denison while experiencing public art and a recreation corridor built directly around the city's Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad heritage.
businesses.why_its_unique: The trail transforms former Katy Railroad right-of-way into a modern shared-use path while celebrating the railroad that played such an important role in Denison's development through six railroad-inspired sculptures.
businesses.hours_note: Dedicated Katy Trail daily operating hours are not currently published. Phase I remains open during the 2026 Phase II improvement project. Beginning May 15, 2026, the Phase II section beyond the pedestrian bridge at Loy Lake extending approximately to Flowers Road is temporarily closed for construction and will remain inaccessible until the City announces reopening.

businesses.verification_note: Fully researched August 15, 2026 after manual TWG live-directory duplicate clearance. The current City of Denison Loy Lake Park facility page confirms the pavilion as a separately reservable lakeside facility within Loy Lake Park at 457 RC Vaughn Rd. The City describes the pavilion as overlooking Loy Lake, with picnic benches and space appropriate for family reunions, birthday parties and casual gatherings. Current rental blocks are 7:00-11:00 AM, 12:00-4:00 PM and 5:00-9:00 PM. Current pricing is $40 per four-hour block for Denison residents and $60 for non-residents, with a $50 refundable deposit. The parent park is open 5:00 AM-11:00 PM daily and includes a lake, nature trails, picnic tables, horseshoe pits, boat access and restrooms. Denison's active RecDesk independently confirms that the pavilion is reservable daily in four-hour blocks, that restrooms are available, and the current advance-booking, cancellation, no-alcohol, special-event and amplification-permit rules. RecDesk spells the street name 'Vaughan' while the City's dedicated Loy Lake Park page spells it 'Vaughn'; TWG uses the dedicated park page's 457 RC Vaughn Rd as canonical while documenting the discrepancy. RecDesk displays 8:00 AM-5:00 PM as facility availability, which conflicts with the City's explicitly published 5:00-9:00 PM rental block, so TWG uses the parent park's operating hours and the explicitly published rental blocks instead. Pavilion capacity, pavilion-specific accessibility and pet rules were not sufficiently confirmed and remain unspecified.

businesses.description: Waterloo Lake Pavilion is a separately reservable covered gathering facility overlooking Waterloo Lake inside Waterloo Lake Regional Park in Denison. businesses.description: Wynne Chapel is a prominent worship, music and special-event venue on the Austin College campus in Sherman. Completed in 1958, the 13,208-square-foot chapel includes the Clifford J. Grum Sanctuary, which seats 600 people on the main level plus 120 in the balcony, as well as the smaller Sallie Majors Chapel, choir rooms, offices, a conference room and a prayer room. The renovated main sanctuary features modern projection, lighting and sound systems while preserving distinctive musical features including an Aeolian-Skinner pipe organ and a 24-bell carillon. Wynne Chapel hosts Austin College worship services, concerts, ceremonies and other campus programs and is also available by reservation for weddings, memorial services and celebrations of life.
businesses.why_visit: Wynne Chapel combines one of Austin College's most recognizable campus spaces with a large performance and gathering venue used for concerts, worship, ceremonies and special community occasions.
businesses.why_its_unique: The chapel pairs a 720-seat sanctuary-and-balcony capacity with an Aeolian-Skinner pipe organ, a 24-bell carillon and renovated modern presentation systems, giving it a distinctive role as both a religious and performing-arts venue.
businesses.hours_note: No regular public walk-in hours are published. Access follows Austin College programs, services and approved reservations. businesses.description: IDEA Center is Austin College's major science, mathematics, engineering and research facility in Sherman. businesses.description: Adams Observatory is Austin College's rooftop astronomy observatory inside the IDEA Center in Sherman. Its silver dome houses a 24-inch research telescope affectionately named Rose after the Yellow Rose of Texas. Austin College identifies the instrument as the largest research telescope in North Texas and equips it with specialized astronomical imaging, planetary imaging and spectroscopy instruments used for teaching and research. The observatory also has direct public value: several times each year Austin College opens Adams Observatory to the campus and wider community for Star Parties, giving visitors opportunities to look through one of the largest telescopes in the region while students share their knowledge of the night sky. The facility also supports significant astronomical research, including Austin College student participation in NASA TESS follow-up work that has helped identify more than 50 exoplanets.
businesses.why_visit: Adams Observatory offers one of Texoma's most distinctive astronomy experiences, giving the public occasional opportunities to look through Austin College's powerful 24-inch research telescope during scheduled Star Parties.
businesses.why_its_unique: The observatory combines serious undergraduate astronomy research with recurring public outreach. Its 24-inch Rose telescope is identified by Austin College as the largest research telescope in North Texas, and student research conducted through the observatory has contributed to the discovery of more than 50 exoplanets.
businesses.hours_note: Adams Observatory is not operated as a regular walk-in attraction. Austin College opens it to the campus and wider public for scheduled Star Parties several times each year. Public access, start times, weather plans and any registration requirements should be confirmed through the current Austin College event listing before visiting.

businesses.description: Ida Green Communication Center is Austin College's dedicated communication, media studies and theatre facility in Sherman. Built in 1972, the 38,372-square-foot center contains multiple performance, exhibition, learning and meeting spaces. Its main 500-seat theatre was extensively renovated beginning in 2020 and reopened as Sally and Jim Nation Theatre, while the renovated first floor also created the Sally and Jim Nation Learning Commons. Other spaces include Paul Beardsley Arena Theatre in the basement, Ida Green Gallery, a student exhibition room and the Cecil Green Conference Suite. Ida Green continues to host performances, exhibitions, lectures, conferences, community celebrations and other Austin College programs.

businesses.description: Robbie Kubela Rogers Lake Campus is Austin College's 30-acre recreational, retreat and camping property on the Preston Peninsula at Lake Texoma near Pottsboro. The lakeside site is primarily available to Austin College students, faculty, staff and alumni for day recreation, meetings, retreats and overnight camping, while non-campus organizations may request the property for approved special events. Facilities include a covered pavilion, seasonal restrooms and showers, designated tent campsites, space for RVs and trailers without utility hookups, fire rings and access to Lake Texoma for swimming and other outdoor recreation. The property was dedicated in 1983 in honor of Austin College trustee Robbie Kubela Rogers, whose support funded numerous improvements to the recreational area.
businesses.why_visit: For eligible Austin College community members or guests attending an approved event, the Lake Campus provides a secluded Lake Texoma setting for camping, retreats, reunions, meetings and outdoor recreation away from the main Sherman campus.
businesses.why_its_unique: Austin College maintains an entire 30-acre Lake Texoma property for its community and approved group events, combining primitive camping, lake recreation and retreat space with a covered pavilion and the ability to accommodate organized non-campus gatherings by reservation.
businesses.hours_note: Standard day use is 9:00 AM-10:00 PM and requires valid Austin College community access. The Lake Campus closes during Opening of School weekend, Thanksgiving break, Christmas/New Year break, Spring Break and ACE. Standard entry ends when the gates close at 10:00 PM. Approved special events may have separate access arrangements. Restroom and shower facilities are generally available from the first Monday after Spring Break until the Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
good_to_know: Routine day use is primarily limited to Austin College students, faculty, staff and alumni and requires valid Austin College identification.
Alumni may obtain a validated access badge through Austin College Campus Police.
Non-campus organizations may request the Lake Campus for approved meetings, retreats, reunions and other special events.
No special-event reservations are accepted on holiday weekends.
Current non-campus event fees are $100 for groups of 25 or fewer, $200 for 26-50, $500 for 51-100 and $1,000 for groups larger than 100.
Non-campus reservations require a non-refundable 50 percent deposit when scheduled, with the remaining balance due one week before the event.
Overnight camping is first-come, first-served rather than individually reserved.
Tent campsites are designated by metal fire rings and are limited to one group and no more than 12 people per site.
RVs, travel trailers and pop-up campers are allowed only around the bathhouse and pavilion area; electrical, water and sewer hookups are not provided.
Camping is limited to seven consecutive nights per visit and 14 nights within a rolling 30-day period.
Swimming is at the visitor's own risk and no lifeguards are provided.
Pets are not allowed for either day use or overnight camping.
Open fires are limited to provided fire pits or cooking grills and are not permitted on the beach.

businesses.description: Craig Hall is the home of the Austin College Department of Music in Sherman and serves as a hub for music education, rehearsals, performances and selected visual-arts programming. Built in 1962, the facility contains classrooms, faculty offices, a music library, rehearsal rooms and the dedicated Craig Recital Hall. The building was intentionally designed for musical acoustics, with sloped ceilings and no rooms whose walls are exactly parallel. Craig Hall also retains an art gallery that continues to host student exhibitions. In addition to everyday academic use, the building supports public student recitals, music scholarship auditions, the Austin College Summer Music Camp and other scheduled arts programs.
